page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with the running head and page number at the top. Below the head, a centred heading "E GRÆCO." Then a four-line poem, then three headed epigrams in italic verse with centred small-capital headings. A short line "AD" at the right edge, cut off by the scan. No notes in the margins.

l.i: Non aurum veluti Gyges: sed illum
Illud nil nimium nimis iuuat me.
Verba Doletus habet (quis nescit?) splendida, verum
Splendida nil praeter verba Doletus habet.
Nil patre cum viuo tibi conueniebat: iniquis
Defunctum nunc thure colis, bustúmque coronas
Quamlibet hic timeas, pietas praepostera certe
est, In patre nil praeter funus amare patris.
Putida vasani referas cum scripta Doleti,
Et blateres nullo iurgia tinɛta sale.
Quicquid agunt alij prae te contemnis & vni
Se tibi dat Phœbus, Pieridèsque fauent.
Solus agas rectè per me licet omnia: sed dum
Omnia te solo iudice solus agas.

page.notes: The right edge is cut off by the scan; the word "AD" at the far right is the start of a following heading and is not transcribed further. The Greek-style heading "E GRÆCO." is set in small capitals. Several words in the poems are set in long-s form in the original; they are given here with plain s. "tinɛta" (line 2 of the third epigram) is doubtful: likely "tincta", the scan is unclear. "dissidiisque" and "senem" are printed as shown with long s, rendered with plain s in the surrounding text.
